decisions.statement: The seven-day quota is 144 hours rather than 168.
Sunday counts toward no part of the seven-day quota.
A Sunday is the day running from midnight to midnight in UTC.
A seven-day window is seven times twenty-four hours rather than seven calendar days.
Elapsed time is measured to the end of the current eso-day rather than to the moment asked about.
A pace is answered at the granularity of a whole day.
The eso-day boundary is taken from the day package rather than worked out again here.
A five-hour window opened five hours before the moment that window resets.
A seven-day window opened seven days before the moment that window resets.
An account whose seven-day reset is unknown has 144 hours until that reset.
A seven-day reset already past answers 144 hours until that reset.
An account whose seven-day reset is unknown has elapsed the whole of its window.
Hours remaining never fall under a thousandth of an hour.
A burn rate is the fraction of the window left over the hours left.
A pace above zero is hours of quota in hand.
A pace is written with a sign and two decimal places.
Every instant this module works from is handed in by the caller.
Nothing here reads a clock.
Nothing here reads a file.
Nothing here reads an index.
Nothing here fetches.
The Sunday left out is a UTC day while a pace is cut at a New York boundary.
The 144 answered for an unknown reset is below the hours a freshly opened window has left.
A pace exactly halfway between two hundredths is rounded toward the greater hundredth.

definition: how far ahead or behind a weekly quota an account is
